Inference for selector via bootstrapping

infer_boot.Rd

Inference for selector via bootstrapping

Usage

infer_boot(
  object,
  data,
  inference_target = c("selections", "all"),
  pad = c("zero_side", "none", "all"),
  conf.level = 0.95,
  type = c("paired", "residual"),
  B = 250,
  n_cores = 4,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

a selector object

data

the data used to fit the selector

inference_target

is inference requested on all or selected only

pad

how to pad the bootstrap percentile intervals, which otherwise collapse toward [0, 0] for small nonzero coefficients the selector rarely picks. Within each replicate a non-selected coefficient is 0.

  • "zero_side" (default): an interval that contains 0 has each endpoint pushed out to at least -delta / delta; intervals that exclude 0 are unchanged. [-delta, delta] is a region of "reasonably confident null" that shrinks with n.

  • "none": the raw percentile interval ("confident nulls").

  • "all": every interval is widened by delta on both sides.

The radius delta is set from the selector (scaled metric) and returned in the null_radius column of tidy():

  • select_ncvreg(): gamma * lambda for MCP/SCAD with "zero_side", lambda with "all".

  • select_glmnet() and lasso select_ncvreg(): lambda. The lasso's bias does not vanish for large effects, so "zero_side" warns; "all" is the uniformly valid choice.

  • select_stepwise_ic(): sqrt(k) times the full-model standard error, with k = 2 (AIC) or log(n) (BIC). Requires n > p + 1.

  • select_full_model() / select_null_model(): 0, so no padding.

Coverage guarantees are for the gaussian family in an orthonormal design; other families warn.

conf.level

.95 by default

type

the bootstrap type. Only "paired" (resampling rows) is implemented; "residual" is reserved and currently an error.

B

number of bootstrap resamples

n_cores

reserved for parallel bootstrapping (see GitHub issue #5). Resampling is currently sequential, so this has no effect, and supplying it warns.

...

not used. Any argument passed here is an error, so that a misspelled or removed argument (such as debias) can't be silently ignored.

Value

an inferrer object; see tidy.inferrer(). Its inferences include prop_selected (the proportion of resamples in which each term was selected) and null_radius (the padding radius; see pad).
